symbols.name: g_n
symbols.def: \(g_{i,n}\) is the first treated period of unit \(i\)

symbols.name: B_n
symbols.def: a disjoint rectangular cover \(W_n=\bigsqcup_{b\in\mathcal B_n}I_b\times Q_b\) with \((I_b\times P_b)\cup(C_b\times P_b)\cup(C_b\times Q_b)\subseteq\Omega_n\)

symbols.name: P_theta_n
symbols.role: full outcome law used by the ATT corollary

symbols.name: Xi_n
symbols.role: Gaussian randomization for independent pilot and inference copies

symbols.name: Zeta_n
symbols.role: independent seed for conditional Gaussian quantile simulation

symbols.name: PrQ_theta_n
symbols.role: joint probability in the observed experiment and over declared procedure randomization

symbols.name: EQ_theta_n
symbols.role: joint expectation in the observed experiment and over declared procedure randomization

symbols.name: PrP_theta_n
symbols.role: joint probability under the full outcome law and over declared procedure randomization

symbols.name: b_0
symbols.def: \(b_0\) is the lexicographically first element of \(\mathcal B_n\)

symbols.name: Pi_r
symbols.def: \(\Pi_r(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{\min\{r,a,b\}}s_j(A)u_j(A)v_j(A)^{\top}\), with deterministic lexicographic signs and bases at ties and with zero singular directions padded when a later factor representation requests \(r\) columns

symbols.name: qf_r
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{qf}_r(H)\) applies exact-arithmetic modified Gram--Schmidt to the ordered list consisting of the \(r\) columns of \(H\), followed by \(e_1,\ldots,e_m\), skips zero residuals, fixes each sign by its first nonzero coordinate, and returns the first \(r\) accepted vectors; this is a measurable fallback when \(H\) is rank deficient

symbols.name: polar_r
symbols.def: if \(A=P\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_r)Q^{\top}\) is the full singular-value decomposition with decreasing singular values and lexicographically selected bases and signs at every tie and zero singular value, then \(\operatorname{polar}_r(A)=PQ^{\top}\)
symbols.role: measurable Procrustes solution on singular as well as nonsingular inputs

symbols.name: G_n
symbols.role: overlap graph for local spectral charts

symbols.name: Jhat_n
symbols.role: plug-in Fr\'{e}chet derivative of block transport

symbols.name: Sigmahat_n
symbols.role: conditional covariance of the Gaussian linearization

symbols.name: Acal_n
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A_n=\{C_{0,n}\times P_{0,n}\}\cup\{C_b\times P_b,(I_b\cup C_b)\times P_{0,n},C_{0,n}\times(P_b\cup Q_b):b\in\mathcal B_n\}\)
symbols.role: observed rectangles used by the pilot

symbols.name: Fall_n
symbols.role: fallback event of the total certificate

symbols.name: mathscr_R_n
symbols.def: \(\mathscr R_n^{(2)}=C_0r^{3/2}\tau_n^2(\widehat\delta_n^{-1}+\widehat M_n\widehat\delta_n^{-2}+\widehat M_n^2\widehat\delta_n^{-3})\) on the stable branch, with the deterministic covering radius on the fallback branch

symbols.name: WSVD_n
symbols.role: total wedge-aware spectral procedure with a balanced one-block rate guarantee

standard.name: spectral diffuseness of a linear functional

novel.justification: A persistent never-treated cohort is present in staggered-adoption applications with late or absent adoption and supplies a common row anchor across cohort charts.
A shared baseline window is natural when every cohort has a common pre-adoption history and makes chart alignment empirically checkable.
The condition requires overlapping cohort charts to form a well-connected synchronization network; common-baseline designs and nested cohort staircases with a persistent donor anchor satisfy it.
Bounded chart incidence is satisfied by coarsened adoption cohorts with bounded overlap multiplicity and prevents a single observed cell from being reused across an increasing number of local fits.

definitions.name: Uniformly honest nuclear-ball procedures
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}=\left\{(\widehat L_n,R_n):(\widehat L_n,R_n)\text{ is measurable in }(X_n,\Xi_n,\Zeta_n),\ R_n\ge0,\ \inf_{\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\in\Theta_n}\Pr_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}\!\left(\lVert P_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L_n)\rVert_*\le R_n\right)\ge1-\alpha\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Two-layer overlap chart synchronization
definitions.construction: Order \(\mathcal B_n\) lexicographically, let \(b_0\) be first, put \(\mathcal V_n=\mathcal B_n\), and compute \(\Pi_r((X_n^{(1)})_{C_bP_b})=\widehat U_b\widehat S_b\widehat V_b^{\top}\), where \(\widehat U_b\in\mathbb R^{|C_b|\times r}\), \(\widehat S_b\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\), and \(\widehat V_b\in\mathbb R^{|P_b|\times r}\), using zero padding and the lexicographic singular bases fixed by \(\Pi_r\) if the observed rank is below \(r\). Join \(b<c\) precisely when \(R_{bc}=C_b\cap C_c\) and \(S_{bc}=P_b\cap P_c\) both have cardinality at least \(r\), and set \(w_{bc}=|R_{bc}|/N_n+|S_{bc}|/T_n\) and \(d_b=\sum_{c:\{b,c\}\in\mathcal E_n}w_{bc}\). The conformable row and column overlap frames are \(H^U_{b,bc}=\operatorname{qf}_r((\widehat U_b)_{R_{bc},\cdot})\in\mathbb R^{|R_{bc}|\times r}\) and \(H^V_{b,bc}=\operatorname{qf}_r((\widehat V_b)_{S_{bc},\cdot})\in\mathbb R^{|S_{bc}|\times r}\). Define \(\widehat O^U_{bc}=\operatorname{polar}_r((H^U_{b,bc})^{\top}H^U_{c,bc})\) and \(\widehat O^V_{bc}=\operatorname{polar}_r((H^V_{b,bc})^{\top}H^V_{c,bc})\), each in \(\mathsf O(r)\), and put \(\widehat O^Z_{cb}=\widehat O^{Z\top}_{bc}\). For \(Z\in\{U,V\}\), the normalized connection Laplacian is the \((r|\mathcal B_n|)\)-square block matrix with \(\mathcal L^Z_{bb}=I_r\), \(\mathcal L^Z_{bc}=-w_{bc}\widehat O^Z_{bc}/\sqrt{d_bd_c}\) on edges, and zero off edges; equivalently it represents the objective \(\sum_{b<c}w_{bc}\lVert Q_b^Z-\widehat O^Z_{bc}Q_c^Z\rVert_F^2\). Select the lexicographically first orthonormal basis of its bottom \(r\)-dimensional eigenspace, block it as \(\widetilde Q_b^Z\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\), set \(\widehat Q_{b_0}^Z=I_r\), and for \(b\ne b_0\) set \(\widehat Q_b^Z=\operatorname{polar}_r(\widetilde Q_b^Z(\widetilde Q_{b_0}^Z)^{\top})\). If a chart core or required overlap has fewer than \(r\) indices, some \(d_b=0\), or the scalar graph is disconnected, the construction returns the global fallback specified in Definition \ref{def:wedge-spectral-procedure}; hence synchronization is defined on every input. When \( |\mathcal B_n|=1\), set \(\widehat Q_{b_0}^U=\widehat Q_{b_0}^V=I_r\), declare the scalar graph connected, and use synchronization amplification one; no normalized-Laplacian eigenvalue is evaluated.

definitions.name: Independent Gaussian pilot and inference copies
definitions.construction: Draw \(\Xi_n\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I_{|\Omega_n|})\) independently of \(X_n\), and set \(X_n^{(1)}=X_n+\Xi_n\) and \(X_n^{(2)}=X_n-\Xi_n\).

definitions.name: Synchronized local spectral pilot
definitions.construction: Run Definition \ref{def:chart-graph}. With \(a_b=|C_b||P_b|\), form the conformable anchor averages \[A_U=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_n}a_b\operatorname{qf}_r((\widehat U_b)_{C_{0,n},\cdot})\widehat Q_b^U\in\mathbb R^{|C_{0,n}|\times r},\qquad A_V=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_n}a_b\operatorname{qf}_r((\widehat V_b)_{P_{0,n},\cdot})\widehat Q_b^V\in\mathbb R^{|P_{0,n}|\times r},\] and set \(\overline U_0=\operatorname{qf}_r(A_U)\) and \(\overline V_0=\operatorname{qf}_r(A_V)\). Let \(\overline K_0=\overline U_0^{\top}(X_n^{(1)})_{C_{0,n}P_{0,n}}\overline V_0\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\), take its lexicographic full singular-value decomposition \(P_0S_0Q_0^{\top}\), and define \(\overline F_0=\overline U_0P_0S_0^{1/2}\in\mathbb R^{|C_{0,n}|\times r}\) and \(\overline G_0=\overline V_0Q_0S_0^{1/2}\in\mathbb R^{|P_{0,n}|\times r}\). Put \(R_b=I_b\cup C_b\) and \(S_b=P_b\cup Q_b\). First compute \(F_b^{(0)}=(X_n^{(1)})_{R_bP_{0,n}}\overline G_0(\overline G_0^{\top}\overline G_0)^{\dagger}\in\mathbb R^{|R_b|\times r}\) and \(G_b^{(0)}=((X_n^{(1)})_{C_{0,n}S_b})^{\top}\overline F_0(\overline F_0^{\top}\overline F_0)^{\dagger}\in\mathbb R^{|S_b|\times r}\). Refine them in the same gauge by \[F_b=(X_n^{(1)})_{R_bP_b}G_{b,P_b}^{(0)}(G_{b,P_b}^{(0)\top}G_{b,P_b}^{(0)})^{\dagger}\in\mathbb R^{|R_b|\times r},\qquad G_b=((X_n^{(1)})_{C_bS_b})^{\top}F_{b,C_b}^{(0)}(F_{b,C_b}^{(0)\top}F_{b,C_b}^{(0)})^{\dagger}\in\mathbb R^{|S_b|\times r}.\] For each row \(i\), let \(\mathcal B_i^F=\{b:i\in R_b\}\), and if nonempty set \(\widetilde F_i=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i^F}\lambda_{ib}^FF_{b,i\cdot}\), where \(\lambda_{ib}^F=|P_b|/\sum_{c\in\mathcal B_i^F}|P_c|\). For each column \(t\), let \(\mathcal B_t^G=\{b:t\in S_b\}\), and if nonempty set \(\widetilde G_t=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_t^G}\lambda_{tb}^GG_{b,t\cdot}\), where \(\lambda_{tb}^G=|C_b|/\sum_{c\in\mathcal B_t^G}|C_c|\). Empty aggregates are the zero row, sums follow lexicographic chart order, and ties in every decomposition use the declared lexicographic rule. Set \(\widetilde X_{it}=\widetilde F_i\widetilde G_t^{\top}\) on \(\Omega_n\) and \(\widetilde X_{it}=0\) on \(W_n\). Finally, use \(\mathcal A_n=\{C_{0,n}\times P_{0,n}\}\cup\{C_b\times P_b,(I_b\cup C_b)\times P_{0,n},C_{0,n}\times(P_b\cup Q_b):b\in\mathcal B_n\}\), all of whose rectangles are observed under the common-anchor design. For \(A\in\mathcal A_n\), set \(\varepsilon_A=\sqrt{2}\sigma\{\sqrt{|\operatorname{row}(A)|}+\sqrt{|\operatorname{col}(A)|}+\sqrt{2\log(8(|\mathcal B_n|+1)/\alpha)}\}\) and \(\varepsilon_n=\max_{A\in\mathcal A_n}\varepsilon_A\). Let \(a_{\mathrm{sync},n}=1\) when \( |\mathcal B_n|=1\), and \(a_{\mathrm{sync},n}=1+d_{\mathrm{chart}}/\gamma_{\mathrm{graph}}\) otherwise, and define the proved post-synchronization envelope \(\tau_n=32a_{\mathrm{sync},n}\varepsilon_n\). Thus the generic second-order bound uses \(\tau_n^2\), which squares the graph amplification. Define \[\widehat\delta_n=\min_{A\in\mathcal A_n}\{s_r((X_n^{(1)})_A)-2\varepsilon_A\}_+,\qquad \widehat M_n=\max_{A\in\mathcal A_n}\{\lVert\Pi_r((X_n^{(1)})_A)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}+\varepsilon_A\}.\]

definitions.name: Common-anchor transport map and derivative
definitions.construction: For \(x\in\mathbb R^{|\Omega_n|}\), set \[(F_n(x))_{I_bQ_b}=x_{I_bP_{0,n}}\{\Pi_r(x_{C_{0,n}P_{0,n}})\}^{\dagger}x_{C_{0,n}Q_b},\qquad b\in\mathcal B_n.\] For a rank-\(r\) matrix \(B=USV^{\top}\), put \(D\Pi_{r,B}[H]=UU^{\top}H+HVV^{\top}-UU^{\top}HVV^{\top}\). For \(f(A,B,C)=A\{\Pi_r(B)\}^{\dagger}C\), define \(Df_{A,B,C}[H_1,H_2,H_3]=H_1B^{\dagger}C+A\,D(B^{\dagger})[D\Pi_{r,B}[H_2]]C+AB^{\dagger}H_3\), where \[D(B^{\dagger})[H]=-B^{\dagger}HB^{\dagger}+B^{\dagger}B^{\dagger\top}H^{\top}(I-BB^{\dagger})+(I-B^{\dagger}B)H^{\top}B^{\dagger\top}B^{\dagger}.\] On the stable branch, assemble the unique coordinate Jacobian \(\widehat J_n=DF_n(\widetilde X_{\Omega_n})\in\mathbb R^{|W_n|\times|\Omega_n|}\) by lexicographic ordering of observed and missing cells.

definitions.name: Total wedge-aware spectral certificate with balanced one-block calibration
definitions.construction: Check from the fixed design that every rectangle in \(\mathcal A_n\) is contained in \(\Omega_n\), that its two dimensions are at least \(r\), that the chart graph is connected under the singleton convention of Definition \ref{def:chart-graph}, that its normalized scalar gap is at least \(\gamma_{\mathrm{graph}}\) when it has more than one vertex, and that the computed chart incidence is at most \(d_{\mathrm{chart}}\). Run Definitions \ref{def:chart-graph}--\ref{def:transport-map}. The stable branch is the event that the design checks hold and \(\widehat\delta_n\ge4\tau_n\); denote its complement by \(\mathcal F_n\). On the stable branch set \[\operatorname{vec}_{W_n}(\widehat L_n)=F_n(\widetilde X_{\Omega_n})+\widehat J_n\{X_n^{(2)}-\widetilde X_{\Omega_n}\},\qquad \widehat\Sigma_n=2\sigma^2\widehat J_n\widehat J_n^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{|W_n|\times|W_n|}.\] Conditional on \(X_n^{(1)}\), \(\widehat J_n\{X_n^{(2)}-\operatorname{vec}_{\Omega_n}(L_n)\}\) is centered Gaussian with covariance \(\widehat\Sigma_n\). Let \(\mathring q_{\alpha,n}\) be the conditional \(1-\alpha/4\) quantile of \(\lVert\operatorname{mat}_{W_n}(\widehat\Sigma_n^{1/2}Z)\rVert_*\), where \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{|W_n|})\). Set \(K_n=\lceil128\alpha^{-2}\log(8n/\alpha)\rceil\) and \(\eta_n=\sqrt{\log(8n/\alpha)/(2K_n)}\). Reading \(\Zeta_n\) in coordinate order, generate \(G_k=\widehat\Sigma_n^{1/2}z_k\) with \(z_k\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,I_{|W_n|})\). Put \(p_n=\min\{1,1-\alpha/4+\eta_n\}\), order \(T_k=\lVert\operatorname{mat}_{W_n}(G_k)\rVert_*\) by value and then simulation index, and set \(\widehat q_{\alpha,n}=T_{(\min\{K_n,\lceil K_np_n\rceil\})}\). Define \[\mathscr R_n^{(2)}=C_0r^{3/2}\tau_n^2\left(\widehat\delta_n^{-1}+\widehat M_n\widehat\delta_n^{-2}+\widehat M_n^2\widehat\delta_n^{-3}\right),\qquad \widehat R_{\alpha,n}=\widehat q_{\alpha,n}+\mathscr R_n^{(2)}.\] On \(\mathcal F_n\), set \(P_{W_n}\widehat L_n=0\), \(\mathscr R_n=s_+\sqrt{r\min\{N_n,T_n\}N_nT_n}\), and \(\widehat R_{\alpha,n}=\mathscr R_n\). The fallback radius deterministically dominates \(\lVert P_{W_n}L_n\rVert_*\). All singular values, pseudoinverses, polar factors, square roots, simulation orderings, and gauges use the total lexicographic conventions already declared, so \(\mathsf{WSVD}_n\) is measurable on every input.

definitions.name: Overlap-aligned tangent-packing handle
definitions.construction: Start from the least singular directions of the cohort overlap Grams, lift them into \(\mathcal T_n(L_n)\), assign a Varshamov--Gilbert sign code across orthogonal cohort charts, and use the fixed-rank exponential-map retraction while bounding the observed Gaussian Kullback--Leibler divergence of the resulting tuple-indexed laws \(\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}\).

statements.statement: For every \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\in\Theta_n\) and every \(b\in\mathcal B_n\), \(\operatorname{rank}(L_{n,C_bP_b})=r\) implies \[L_{n,I_bQ_b}=L_{n,I_bP_b}L_{n,C_bP_b}^{\dagger}L_{n,C_bQ_b}.\] Hence the tuple-indexed missing-block mean is a functional of the observed mean under \(\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}\).
statements.justification: The identity supplies the algebraic map used by the benchmark certificate and is not itself the novelty claim.
statements.gap: Bai and Ng use tall-wide rotation for imputation but do not make this tuple-indexed block identity the basis of an honest nuclear ball.
statements.consumer: The synchronized spectral certificate uses the identity to combine observed blocks while keeping the latent target attached to the experiment index.

statements.statement: Under the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask assumptions, there exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(\mu\), \(\kappa\), \(s_-\), and \(s_+\), such that for all sufficiently large even \(n\), \[c\sigma\sqrt n\le\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\le C\sigma\sqrt n.\] The upper bound is attained by the total polynomial-time one-block procedure \(\mathsf{WSVD}_n\), whose conditional Gaussian, finite-simulation, homogeneous Taylor, and fallback contributions are each \(O(\sigma\sqrt n)\). The lower bound holds for every procedure uniformly honest over all tuples \(\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n\).
statements.justification: The benchmark distinguishes collective low-rank uncertainty from the order-\(n\) radius obtained by summing entrywise intervals.
statements.gap: Yan and Wainwright prove sharp scalar widths, and Capponi and Stojnic characterize Frobenius residuals of one algorithm; neither gives an all-procedure tuple-indexed honest nuclear-radius frontier.
statements.consumer: Researchers can report a simultaneous uncertainty set for the entire treated counterfactual block at a sub-diameter scale.

statements.statement: For every \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\in\Theta_n\), conditional on the fixed design, \(X_n^{(1)}\) and \(X_n^{(2)}\) are independent and each has distribution \(\mathcal N(\operatorname{vec}_{\Omega_n}(L_n),2\sigma^2I_{|\Omega_n|})\).
statements.justification: The independent copy makes the conditional covariance calibration exact once the pilot is fixed.
statements.gap: The four-block literature uses leave-one-out expansions; the randomized Gaussian split gives an exact conditional experiment for a joint nuclear certificate.
statements.consumer: The certificate uses the inference copy for a conditionally Gaussian one-step correction and the pilot copy for synchronization.

statements.statement: For every fixed design and realization of \((X_n,\Xi_n,\Zeta_n)\), \(\mathsf{WSVD}_n\) returns one measurable pair \((\widehat L_n,\widehat R_{\alpha,n})\). On the stable branch, \(\widehat J_n\in\mathbb R^{|W_n|\times|\Omega_n|}\), \(\widehat\Sigma_n=2\sigma^2\widehat J_n\widehat J_n^{\top}\) is positive semidefinite, \(\widehat q_{\alpha,n}\) is a finite order statistic, and the homogeneous \(\mathscr R_n^{(2)}\) is finite and observable. Every failed design, rank, or stability check returns the declared finite fallback. The arithmetic cost is polynomial in \(N_n\), \(T_n\), \(|\mathcal B_n|\), and \(\alpha^{-1}\).
statements.justification: Totality and dimensional conformity are prerequisites for treating the displayed certificate as a statistical procedure.
statements.gap: Existing local four-block algorithms do not specify a globally synchronized, all-input covariance-and-quantile map.
statements.consumer: The honesty theorem can quantify over the procedure without excluding singular samples or leaving implementation choices implicit.

statements.statement: Under the balanced rank-one one-chart assumptions, the synchronization gauge is \(1\) and no graph transport is performed. On \(\mathcal G_n\), every local spectral, anchor-regression, deterministic aggregation, and completed pilot block used by \(F_n\) has operator-norm error at most \(\tau_n=32\varepsilon_n\). In particular, the post-synchronization envelope is homogeneous of noise order \(\tau_n=O(\sigma\sqrt n)\).
statements.justification: The one-chart calculation isolates the exact perturbation scale before nonlinear block transport.
statements.gap: Published four-block analyses control scalar entries; this lemma records the joint operator envelope required by a nuclear-radius Taylor bound.
statements.consumer: The balanced radius audit substitutes this envelope into every first- and second-order certificate term.

statements.statement: Under the balanced rank-one one-chart assumptions, there are constants \(c_1,C_1,C_2<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha,\mu,\kappa,s_-,s_+\), such that, uniformly over \(\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n\), \[\mathbb E[\mathring q_{\alpha,n}]\le C_1\sigma\sqrt n,\qquad \mathbb E[(\widehat q_{\alpha,n}-\mathring q_{\alpha,n})_+]\le C_1\sigma\sqrt n,\qquad \mathbb E[\widehat q_{\alpha,n}]\le C_2\sigma\sqrt n.\] On \(\mathcal G_n\cap\mathcal F_n^c\), \(\widehat\delta_n\asymp s_-n\), \(\widehat M_n=O(s_+n)\), and therefore \[\mathscr R_n^{(2)}\le C_2\frac{\sigma^2}{s_-}\le C_2\sigma\sqrt n,\qquad \mathbb E[\mathscr R_n^{(2)}\mathbf 1\{\mathcal F_n^c\}]\le C_2\sigma\sqrt n.\] Moreover, for all sufficiently large even \(n\), \[\Pr(\mathcal F_n)\le C_1\exp\{-c_1s_-^2n/\sigma^2\}\le C_2\frac{\sigma}{s_+n},\qquad s_+n^{3/2}\Pr(\mathcal F_n)\le C_2\sigma\sqrt n.\] The first display separately bounds the exact conditional Gaussian term and its finite-simulation inflation. The other displays follow from the large population chart gap of order \(s_-n\), a Gaussian operator-norm tail evaluated at that gap, the stability test \(\widehat\delta_n\ge4\tau_n\), and the homogeneous identity \(\mathscr R_n^{(2)}=C_0\tau_n^2(\widehat\delta_n^{-1}+\widehat M_n\widehat\delta_n^{-2}+\widehat M_n^2\widehat\delta_n^{-3})\). Thus synchronization, Monte Carlo calibration, Taylor remainder, and fallback contributions each have order at most \(\sigma\sqrt n\) without cancellation.
statements.justification: A termwise benchmark audit rules out a formally honest but diameter-scale expected radius.
statements.gap: Neither scalar staggered-panel inference nor Frobenius residual theory audits conditional nuclear quantiles, nonlinear remainder, simulation, and fallback on one common scale.
statements.consumer: The benchmark certificate and two-sided minimax theorem use these four bounds without cancellation.

statements.statement: Under the balanced rank-one one-chart assumptions, for all sufficiently large even \(n\), the total algorithm \(\mathsf{WSVD}_n\) is randomized polynomial-time and \[(\widehat L_n,\widehat R_{\alpha,n})\in\mathcal H_{\alpha,n},\qquad \sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}[\widehat R_{\alpha,n}]\le C\sigma\sqrt n,\] where \(C\) depends only on \(\alpha,\mu,\kappa,s_-,s_+\). Honesty includes every singular or failed-stability sample through the deterministic fallback, and the expected-radius assertion follows by adding the separately controlled conditional Gaussian, simulation, homogeneous Taylor, and fallback terms in Lemma \ref{lem:balanced-radius-audit}.
statements.justification: This benchmark-only lemma supplies the constructive half of the field-grade minimax frontier.
statements.gap: Existing results do not give a total polynomial-time honest nuclear ball with every expected-radius component verified at the balanced L-mask scale.
statements.consumer: The principal frontier theorem uses this certificate for its upper bound.

statements.statement: For every \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\in\Theta_n\) under the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask assumptions and every deterministic \(A_n\) satisfying treated support, normalization, nonnegativity, and diffuseness, \[\Pr_{\mathbb P_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}\{\tau_{A,n}\in\mathrm{CI}_{A,n}\}\ge1-\alpha.\] The half-length is at most \(a_n\widehat R_{\alpha/2,n}+z_{1-\alpha/4}\sigma\lVert A_n\rVert_F\); this is a coverage result from nuclear--operator duality, not an optimal-length assertion.
statements.justification: Nuclear/operator duality transfers the global counterfactual certificate to a pre-specified diffuse ATT, while the independent treated-cell noise is covered separately.
statements.gap: Functional-specific papers derive sharper tailored laws; this result is solely a coverage-valid duality corollary.
statements.consumer: Applied staggered-adoption studies can reuse the global matrix uncertainty set for one valid weighted ATT interval.

statements.statement: For the full tuple space \(\Theta_n\), without the balanced one-block restriction and without common anchors, graph-gap, or bounded-incidence restrictions beyond quantitative overlap Grams, is there a randomized polynomial-time procedure \((\widehat L_n,R_n)\in\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}\) and a constant \(c>0\) such that \[\sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}[R_n]\lesssim\mathfrak R_n\quad\text{and}\quad\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\ge c\mathfrak R_n?\] The handle is an overlap-aligned tangent packing in the tuple-indexed experiment, paired with nonorthogonal transport or synchronization on the unanchored chart graph.
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing open content needed for a matched all-wedge minimax characterization rather than a common-anchor upper theorem.
statements.gap: Carpentier and Nickl use isotropic trace-regression mixtures, while Yan and Wainwright use scalar local bounds; neither treats exact-rank tuple-indexed alternatives over every deterministic staircase.
statements.consumer: A positive answer would determine when global counterfactual uncertainty is intrinsic to the wedge rather than to a particular synchronization scheme.

sampling_model.design: The schedule \(g_n\), wedge \(\Omega_n\), dimensions, rank, and noise variance are fixed and known. The rate-optimal constructive theorem is restricted to the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask.
sampling_model.units: The parameter at index \(n\) is the tuple \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\) in \(\Theta_n\), not an observational equivalence class of outcome laws.
sampling_model.treatment: The matrix \(D_n\) is supported on \(W_n\); the counterfactual target is the \(L_n\) coordinate of the same experiment index.
sampling_model.overlap: The full class imposes quantitative observed-subblock Grams. The proved rate certificate uses the single balanced chart, for which the row and column anchors are the observed half-panels and synchronization is the identity.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The total procedure randomizes the observed vector into independent Gaussian pilot and inference copies, uses total spectral and pseudoinverse conventions, applies one-step block transport, and calibrates an explicitly ordered conditional Gaussian nuclear quantile plus the homogeneous observable remainder \(\mathscr R_n^{(2)}\). The stable branch requires \(\widehat\delta_n\ge4\tau_n\); every failure triggers a deterministic covering radius. The \(\sigma\sqrt n\) expected-radius guarantee is asserted only for the balanced one-chart benchmark.
sampling_model.randomness: Under \(\mathbb P_{\vartheta,n}\), cells are independent \(\mathcal N(L_{n,it}+D_{n,it},\sigma^2)\); the main observed experiment is its \(P_{\Omega_n}Y_n\) marginal \(\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give entrywise Gaussian inference and a matching scalar instance-wise lower bound under staggered adoption.
Theorems 1 and 4 derive nuclear detection boundaries and nuclear-diameter rank-adaptation impossibility in Gaussian trace regression.
Theorems 3.4--3.5 characterize worst-case Frobenius residual error for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block.
Proposition 2 derives tall-wide common-component error expansions under strong factors in the observed subblocks.
The paper constructs prescribed-coverage intervals for individual effects and bilinear functionals under staggered adoption.
The paper gives rate-optimal recovery and asymptotic normality for average treatment effects under general intervention patterns.

tldr: The paper indexes the Gaussian panel experiment by admissible tuples \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\), so the latent counterfactual matrix remains part of the experiment index even when tuples induce the same observed law. Its principal field-grade result is the balanced rank-one L-mask frontier \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\sqrt n\). A total polynomial-time one-block certificate uses randomized Gaussian splitting, exact block transport, a conditional Gaussian nuclear quantile, and the homogeneous remainder \(C_0\tau_n^2(\widehat\delta_n^{-1}+\widehat M_n\widehat\delta_n^{-2}+\widehat M_n^2\widehat\delta_n^{-3})\), with stability threshold \(\widehat\delta_n\ge4\tau_n\). A large-gap Gaussian tail makes the fallback contribution \(O(\sigma\sqrt n)\), and every other radius component passes the same scale separately. Matching the tangent modulus over arbitrary admissible wedges remains open. The diffuse-weight ATT interval is only a coverage-valid duality corollary.

project_justification.gap: Sharp staggered-panel inference is coordinatewise or functional-specific, while global matrix confidence theory uses random or isotropic measurements. No located result gives a tuple-indexed honest nuclear ball under a deterministic adoption wedge with a computable spectral radius and an all-procedure benchmark.
project_justification.niche: Known rank, independent Gaussian cells, strong factors, quantitative overlap Grams, and the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask isolate the first nontrivial global nuclear-loss benchmark.
project_justification.fill: The principal theorem proves the \(\sigma\sqrt n\) two-sided frontier. Its total spectral certificate is audited term by term, including a squared synchronization amplification in the homogeneous Taylor remainder and a genuine large-gap fallback tail. The overlap-aligned tangent-packing question isolates the unmatched arbitrary-wedge extension.

related_work: Yan and Wainwright provide the closest computational and inferential construction: their four-block SVD estimator has non-asymptotic entrywise Gaussian approximations and matching scalar lower bounds. Bai and Ng supply the tall-wide factor-rotation architecture and asymptotic counterfactual expansions under strong observed subblocks; block transport is used here as a supporting identification lemma. Carpentier and Nickl supply a testing reduction for honest nuclear confidence diameter, but their experiment is isotropic Gaussian trace regression and their central obstruction is rank adaptation. Capponi and Stojnic analyze worst-case Frobenius residuals and phase transitions for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block; their loss and procedure-specific target differ from the uniformly honest radius. Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan provide debiased uncertainty quantification under random sampling, where sampling isometry replaces deterministic block geometry. Chatterjee characterizes qualitative recoverability under arbitrary deterministic masks. Arkhangelsky and Imbens organize factor and assignment-pattern distinctions but report no global honest matrix radius. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright and Farias, Li, and Peng are functional-specific benchmarks for weighted effects; the ATT proposition claims coverage transfer and no optimal-length comparison.
technical_internal_limitation: The \(\sigma\sqrt n\) certificate and minimax frontier are confined to the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask. The displayed multi-chart synchronization remains a total computational construction, but no rate or honesty theorem is asserted for a general connected wedge. A broader theorem would need a uniform post-synchronization envelope and nuclear-mask amplification bound, together with a same-class tangent packing that preserves exact rank, strong factors, incoherence, and controlled observed-law divergence.
honest_scope: The balanced rank-one two-sided frontier, its total one-block spectral certificate, and the diffuse-weight ATT coverage corollary are theorem targets. The exact conditional Gaussian term, Monte Carlo inflation, homogeneous Taylor remainder, and fallback contribution are each bounded at the \(\sigma\sqrt n\) benchmark scale. Both a polynomial-time rate-optimal certificate and a matching all-procedure lower bound for arbitrary quantitatively admissible wedges remain open in Open-ended Question 1. No theorem is asserted for a multi-chart connected wedge, unknown rank, approximate low rank, dependent or heteroskedastic errors, adaptive adoption, or optimal ATT length. In the noiseless one-chart case, the supporting block-transport lemma reduces to exact tall-wide transport.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Theorems 1--2 in Section 4.1, and Section 7
seed_details.proof_boundary: The published lower bound is scalar and genie-aided; the first changed step is a restriction-preserving Gaussian testing construction whose alternatives accumulate nuclear separation across the entire missing block.
seed_details.destination_search: A search for fixed-mask, known-rank, nuclear-norm confidence balls found trace-regression adaptation results and random-completion inference, but no deterministic L-mask result.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from entrywise instance-optimal intervals by summation.
seed_details.rebuttal: Summation loses the shared rank-one row and column directions and gives an order-\(n\) radius, whereas the proposed theorem targets order \(\sigma\sqrt n\) and requires a collective all-procedure lower bound.

seed_details.anchor_location: Algorithm 2, Section 4.2, and the leave-one-block-out discussion in Section 7
seed_details.proof_boundary: The published assembly is coordinatewise; the changed step is a total randomized split, joint conditional Gaussian nuclear calibration, a homogeneous second-order remainder, and a large-gap fallback analysis for the balanced one-block chart.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing staggered adoption with a global nuclear confidence radius returned only entrywise, bilinear-functional, or random-mask uncertainty quantification.
seed_details.red_team: A triangle inequality over the published four-block intervals already gives the certificate.
seed_details.rebuttal: A triangle inequality over entrywise intervals gives an order-\(n\) radius; the benchmark certificate instead calibrates the shared low-rank block error jointly and audits every term at order \(\sigma\sqrt n\).

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Assumptions A--C, Proposition 2, and Section 6
seed_details.proof_boundary: The balanced one-block theorem supplies a solved benchmark; the first unresolved step is either proving a uniform multi-chart synchronization and nuclear-mask amplification bound or constructing same-class tangent alternatives showing graph amplification is unavoidable.
seed_details.destination_search: No located deterministic-mask result makes finite overlap-Gram spectra an if-and-only-if invariant for honest nuclear uncertainty.
seed_details.red_team: The Gram eigenvalues merely restate the tall-wide strong-factor assumption.
seed_details.rebuttal: Sufficiency is implicit in block transport, but necessity for a global nuclear radius and completeness of this finite invariant across multi-cohort wedges are not established.

seed_details.seed: Joint nuclear-error limit law for four-block transport
seed_details.proof_boundary: The scalar Gaussian coupling must be replaced at the first projection step by a joint low-rank Gaussian matrix approximation and a singular-value delta method.
seed_details.destination_search: Random-mask debiasing papers give finite collections of entrywise or factor confidence regions, not a trace-norm limit under an L-mask.
seed_details.red_team: The continuous mapping theorem applied to the published Gaussian expansion gives the result.
seed_details.rebuttal: The expansion is entrywise rather than uniform in the growing missing block, and the nuclear norm is nondifferentiable at the shared low-rank Gaussian limit.

seed_details.seed: Known-rank nuclear efficiency bound under a deterministic wedge
seed_details.proof_boundary: The trace-regression likelihood has isotropic information; the first changed step is deriving the semiparametric tangent norm for a deterministic coordinate projection with a curved rank manifold.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found Bayesian Cram\'{e}r--Rao bounds for one missing entry, but no efficiency bound for the nonsmooth nuclear loss of a missing block.
seed_details.red_team: Nuclear loss has no regular influence function, so an efficiency bound is ill-posed.
seed_details.rebuttal: A local asymptotic minimax bound for the loss is meaningful, but the lack of a canonical regular scalar functional makes this lane less clean than the honest-radius formulation.

seed_details.seed: Conformal inversion of a low-rank counterfactual matrix path
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is finding a valid symmetry orbit for factor residual matrices under deterministic staggered missingness.
seed_details.destination_search: Counterfactual conformal methods use time permutations or placebo units, but the strong-factor model with independent cell noise already provides a more direct Gaussian route.
seed_details.red_team: Exact Gaussian noise makes conformal inversion an unnecessarily indirect calibration device.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the stated topic, which fixes the Gaussian experiment.

seed_details.anchor_location: Section 4 treatment-effect expansions, Proposition 4, and Section 6
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is optimizing the dual nuclear-ball radius against a direct functional influence variance over a class of weight matrices.
seed_details.destination_search: Direct ATT and bilinear-functional procedures occupy functional-specific optimality, while no paper located characterizes when one global nuclear ball is rate-competitive.
seed_details.red_team: Nuclear/operator duality makes the interval-length result immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coverage transfer is immediate and is retained only as a corollary; statistical competitiveness against direct functional inference would require a separate lower bound and is not claimed as the kernel.

seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is replacing independent cohortwise rotation choices by one least-squares synchronization over the overlap graph.

seed_details.red_team: Rotation synchronization is standard multi-view PCA.
seed_details.rebuttal: Standard synchronization does not provide an observable honest radius or account for the anisotropic deterministic wedge, so it is a method component rather than a complete kernel.

seed_details.seed: Approximately low-rank honest nuclear oracle inequality
seed_details.proof_boundary: Their residual optimization treats worst-case Frobenius error of nuclear-norm minimization; the first changed step is separating approximation bias from stochastic nuclear uncertainty under uniform coverage.
